subject: Invoice line-item mapping & tiered commit — vendor form questions
messages:
From: Lydia Chen <lydia.chen@novatech.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Novatech Procurement <procurement@novatech.com>
Date: 2027-04-10T16:12:00Z
Subject: Vendor form — pricing structure questions

Jordan — thanks for the demo last week. Procurement is trying to load Redwood as a preferred supplier but ran into a couple of issues with the vendor form and the way our finance tools expect invoicing. High level:

- Our vendor form does not accept "usage credits" or negative line items. It wants SKUs, unit price, and quantity per invoice.
- We cannot reconcile a per-token variable line item unless there's a capped commit or a monthly true-up workflow with sample invoice mapping.

Could you send: (a) a sample invoice showing how Redwood would map token-based charges to GL codes and line items, (b) proposed SKU names / quantities we should enter on the vendor form for a typical commit tier, and (c) a clear statement of overage rates and liability cap?

We also need SOC 2 attestation and a filled vendor form file in PDF so our Sourcing team can run it through the approval workflow. Goal is to present to the committee on Apr 20.

Thanks,
Lydia Chen
Procurement Manager | Novatech
Lydia.Chen@novatech.com
+1 415 555 0198

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Lydia Chen <lydia.chen@novatech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-12T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Vendor form — pricing structure questions

Lydia — thanks for the note and the timeline. Attached are two files to start: a filled vendor form PDF we completed with suggested SKUs (Novatech_VendorForm_Filled.pdf) and a price sheet (ratecard-v2.xlsx) that maps our per-token model into discrete invoiceable line items. Summary of the approach we recommend:

1) Create a "Tiered Prepaid Commitment" SKU per contract year (e.g., TIER-100M-TOKENS). That SKU has a single unit price and a quantity that represents the pre-purchased token bucket. Invoice line: "Tiered Prepaid Commitment — 100,000,000 tokens" with quantity 1 and total price = agreed commit.
2) On monthly invoices, list: (a) amortized portion of the prepaid commitment (optional), (b) usage reconciliation line showing tokens consumed against the bucket with a second line for overage where applicable (SKU: OVERAGE-1M-TOKENS).
3) Overage SKU with fixed per-1M token price. If overage occurs, we invoice the overage SKU quantity equal to overage tokens / 1,000,000.
4) Unused prepaid tokens can be carried forward for up to 90 days (we propose) or refunded at the end of term — happy to negotiate.

Attachments include a sample-invoice-usage-mapping.pdf that shows how the lines would look in QuickBooks/NetSuite GL-friendly format. For SOC 2 and attestation, I'll loop in compliance but can share the cert PDF immediately if that helps.

If the vendor form still rejects the prepaid SKU idea, we can instead propose an annual fixed invoice plus a monthly reconciliation credit/charge. Which is easier for your AP?

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com
(650) 555-0123

Attachment: Novatech_VendorForm_Filled.pdf, ratecard-v2.xlsx, sample-invoice-usage-mapping.pdf

From: Novatech Procurement <procurement@novatech.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Lydia Chen <lydia.chen@novatech.com>
Date: 2027-04-14T09:33:00Z
Subject: Re: Vendor form — pricing structure questions

Jordan — appreciate the quick turnaround. A few points from Sourcing/Finance after looking at the attachments:

- Our vendor intake system cannot accept bundled "commitment" as a single SKU with a conditional carry-forward; it expects a price-per-unit + quantity per invoice. If you enter a single-item invoice for a prepaid commitment it will break various GL mappings unless you supply a standard reconciliation file each month.
- We cannot accept negative "credit" lines labeled as adjustments; credits must be documented as a refund or a separate vendor credit memo process.
- For reconciliation, we require an example file (CSV) mapping token consumption to your invoice line SKUs and the GL codes we must use. 

Two asks to unblock approval: (1) Provide an example CSV of monthly reconciliation showing token delta and the resulting invoice lines (you referenced sample-invoice-usage-mapping.pdf but Procurement needs a machine-readable CSV example), and (2) re-fill the vendor form using discrete SKUs for commit buckets + overage SKUs with explicit unit sizes and unit prices (no free-text conditional fields).

Also, final ask: what is Redwood's maximum annual liability (we use this in the vendor approval process) and can you confirm the SOC 2 date/version? Procurement meeting Apr 20 — need materials by EOD Apr 15 to be included.

Regards,
Novatech Procurement Team
procurement@novatech.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Novatech Procurement <procurement@novatech.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Lydia Chen <lydia.chen@novatech.com>
Date: 2027-04-15T14:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Vendor form — pricing structure questions

Hi Lydia / Procurement — jumping in from Sales Ops to propose a format that should work in most vendor intake systems. Please see attached draft (vendor-form-draft-for-novatech.pdf). Key changes from Jordan's first pass:

- Split the prepaid commitment into discrete SKUs by unit size (e.g., SKU: COMMIT-10M, COMMIT-50M, COMMIT-100M). Each SKU has a fixed unit price and you enter quantity = number of SKUs purchased (usually 1). This avoids a negative/credit line on the vendor form.
- Add an explicit Overage SKU: OVERAGE-1M (unit price = $X per 1,000,000 tokens). Invoices should report overage as a separate payable line.
- Provide a monthly reconciliation CSV template (attached sample) and an automated GL mapping example (we can send format for NetSuite or QuickBooks).
- Proposed liability cap for commercial terms: standard Redwood T&Cs (we'll provide a short statement) — we can also accept a contract clause limiting liability to fees paid in the prior 12 months for this deal if that helps your committee.

If this looks acceptable I can produce a PDF of the vendor form pre-filled with your company name and the chosen SKU options. Also attaching a sample-invoice-usage-mapping.csv for Procurement to ingest.

Marissa Cole
Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

Attachments: vendor-form-draft-for-novatech.pdf, sample-invoice-usage-mapping.csv

From: Lydia Chen <lydia.chen@novatech.com>

Subject: Re: Vendor form — pricing structure questions

Marissa / Jordan — thanks for the updated draft and the CSV sample. This is much closer to what Procurement needs. A few final items before we can greenlight: 

- Confirm the per-1M token overage price in writing and confirm whether volume discounts apply to overage SKUs once a certain monthly threshold is crossed.
- We need the SOC 2 Type II cert (date and report ID) attached to the vendor form PDF.
- We will accept the "liability cap = fees paid in prior 12 months" option; please confirm in a one-paragraph statement we can paste into the vendor form.
- Once you provide the short liability statement and the SOC 2 PDF, we will route the updated vendor form to legal and include it in the Apr 20 packet. If everything is OK, Procurement will request DocuSign signatures next week.

Please send the two items by EOD Apr 19 and we can proceed.

Thanks,
Lydia
Procurement Manager | Novatech
